clue.text: It measures two attributes of a gymnast

parts.note: a gymnast needs bounce, a lively leap off the floor
a gymnast also needs poise and steadiness on the beam

explanation.surface: A judge's scorecard rating a gymnast on two qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: The two qualities are simply set side by side; the whole phrase then names a weighing device that uses a coiled metal piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighing instrument using a coiled metal piece is a device for gauging weight, so it is something that measures.

clue.text: Bill goes to the North gate

parts.note: a bill is a placard or notice stuck on a wall
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A man named Bill heads off to the northern gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a placard.
explanation.definitionFit: A small back or side entrance to a castle or town wall is this kind of gate.

clue.text: Might be in or even out

indicators.note: 'might be' says the letters of 'in or' could be formed into a different word

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something that could be inside or outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might be' rearranges the four letters of 'in or'.
explanation.definitionFit: To press creases flat is to smooth or level a fabric, which is evening it out.

clue.text: Aviation spirit

parts.note: reads like aircraft fuel, but means an imp that RAF airmen blamed for mechanical faults

explanation.definitionFit: Airmen in the Second World War blamed unexplained engine trouble on mischievous imps, so such a sprite is an aviation spirit.

clue.text: Trainee goes round Grand National course

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters of the word trainee are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A new stable lad walks the course of Britain's most famous steeplechase.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase horse race, run near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse near Liverpool where the Grand National steeplechase is run each spring.

clue.text: An entrance I'd turn in at

indicators.note: in says the turned letters go inside the word at

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the two letters of I'd backwards

parts.note: the letters of I'd without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone says they would go in at a particular doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An entrance' sounds like a doorway; an adit is a horizontal mine passage. 'turn' reverses I'd and 'in' places that inside AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal passage driven into a hillside to reach a mine is a way in, an entrance.

clue.text: One may peg out playing it

definitions.text: One may peg out playing it

parts.words: One may peg out playing it
parts.note: 'peg out' sounds like dying, but in this lawn game a player finishes by hitting the ball against the central peg

explanation.definitionFit: In this lawn game with mallets and hoops, a ball finishes by striking the winning peg, called pegging out.

clue.text: Site for an open-air theatre?

parts.note: the theatre is not for plays but an operating theatre set up outdoors near a battle

explanation.definitionFit: A temporary military medical unit near the front line holds operating theatres in the open country, under canvas.

clue.text: Stake all on success when there's little choice at the butchers?

definitions.text: when there's little choice at the butchers?

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means risking everything on one attempt; jokingly, a butcher offering only one cut of meat or none at all leaves little choice.

clue.text: Available to customers, or about to arrive

explanation.definitionFit: Goods held in a shop are on sale to shoppers; something coming soon is waiting for you, in the future.

clue.text: Offensive rumour about a retired doctor

indicators.note: about tells us the rumour word goes round the turned doctor

parts.note: noise can mean talk or rumour, as in making noises about something

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the doctor's letters go backwards

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A nasty piece of gossip concerning a doctor who has stopped practising.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (Medical Officer) is the standard crossword doctor; 'retired' reverses it and 'about' wraps the rumour word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a foul smell or that is thoroughly disagreeable is nasty, giving offence.

clue.text: Falsified one's accounts?

parts.note: suggests fiddling the books, but simply means told untruths when giving one's version of events

explanation.definitionFit: Telling untruths in one's account of events is a past-tense way of falsifying, or fibbing.

clue.text: Highlight of 70s fashion trousers?

parts.note: a bright light signal, and also the widened bottom of the bell-bottom trousers popular in the 1970s

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a burst of bright light used as a signal and the widening at the foot of bell-bottomed trousers.

clue.text: When bulbs come to life?

parts.note: bulbs seem to be flowers sprouting, but they are light bulbs switched on at nightfall

explanation.definitionFit: Evening twilight is the time of day when people switch on electric lamps.

clue.text: The remains of a sporting trophy

explanation.definitionFit: Burnt remains are what fire leaves; also the urn contested in England-Australia cricket test series.

clue.text: Port and orange

explanation.definitionFit: An ancient harbour town now part of Tel Aviv, also the name of a sweet orange variety grown there.

clue.text: Keeps going, or waits

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means persists stubbornly, and also holds the line while waiting.

clue.text: Once in the theatre, he demands his moneysworth

parts.note: ex means former, once
a player who works on the stage is an actor

explanation.surface: A one-time stage performer insists on value for his money.
explanation.walkthrough: Together the two pieces say a former stage player; the definition reads the whole as one who extracts payment.
explanation.definitionFit: One who insists on full payment or extorts what is due is a demander of value.

clue.text: Reserve player gets no score-with very chilly result

parts.note: a sub is a substitute on the bench
zero is nil, no score

explanation.surface: A substitute fails to score, which leaves the team frozen out.
explanation.definitionFit: Below freezing point on the thermometer means extremely cold.

clue.text: Swell watering place

explanation.definitionFit: To rise up in a bubble on the skin is to swell; jokingly such a bubble is a place full of watery fluid.

clue.text: One who is against work has a problem

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: Someone resisting the job finds a difficulty in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who resists or argues against something is an opponent.

clue.text: N. America's largest meat producer

parts.note: sounds like a big food company, but means the continent's biggest land animal, the bison

explanation.definitionFit: The bison is the heaviest land mammal of North America and a source of meat.

clue.text: Made a come-back after hitting bottom

definitions.text: Made a come-back after hitting bottom

parts.words: Made a come-back after hitting bottom
parts.note: reads like a recovery from despair, but describes a ball rebounding off the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A ball that rebounds off the floor springs back up after striking the ground.

clue.text: Cast pie out, though it's germ-free

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of cast pie are put out of order

explanation.surface: A pie is thrown away even though it is perfectly clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the seven letters of CAST PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Free from bacteria and infection, as surgical instruments must be: sterile.

clue.text: One king is showing the flag

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
R stands for Rex, Latin king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single monarch is flying the national banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is the yellow flag, a wild flower, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild waterside plant of this genus with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Start to speak out as an orator?

definitions.text: Start to speak out as an orator?

parts.words: Start to speak out as an orator?
parts.note: suggests a hesitant first word, but describes holding forth at length as a speech-maker does

explanation.definitionFit: To declaim at length in a pompous way is how a windy speech-maker talks.

clue.text: Become engaged in some sharp practice

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the phrase some sharp

explanation.surface: Getting betrothed through a bit of underhand dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become engaged' is gears interlocking, not a betrothal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth interlock when they engage, fitting together.

clue.text: Bargain for crop

explanation.definitionFit: A cheap purchase is a steal; to cut short with scissors is to trim or clip.

clue.text: Such a fuss getting to the party

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a social gathering or party

explanation.surface: Arriving at the celebration causes great commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or bother over something is a fuss.

clue.text: Comes to school and listens

explanation.definitionFit: Goes regularly to classes, and also pays heed to what is said.

clue.text: One of the toasts that may be offered with a meal

definitions.text: One of the toasts that may be offered with a meal

parts.words: One of the toasts that may be offered with a meal
parts.note: toasts suggests raised glasses and speeches, but means small cubes of fried bread served with soup

explanation.definitionFit: A small cube of fried or crisped bread garnishes soup or salad at dinner.

clue.text: Resolute drama students are

explanation.definitionFit: Ready and determined to take action; jokingly, drama pupils are trained to perform on stage.
